newsitem.title: INDIA: India's LG-Hotline sets up $61 mln plant.
newsitem.headline: India's LG-Hotline sets up $61 mln plant.

text.p: India's LG-Hotline CPT Ltd has set up the country's largest television tube plant at a cost of 2.2 billion rupees ($ 61.45 million), a company official said on Monday.

LG-Hotline is a 50:50 joint venture between India's Hotline Glass Ltd and South Korea's LG Electronics. A television tube constitutes 45 percent of a television or computer monitor's raw material cost.
The company's plant is located in the central Indian state of Madhya Pradesh and will produce 1.4 million tubes annually at full capacity.

"The full investment of 2.2 billion rupees has been made in the plant. Trial production commenced in January this year, and commercial production began in April," D.C. Mathur, vice president (finance) at LG-Hotline, told Reuters.
The promoters, Hotline and LG have invested 450 million rupees each as equity capital. The rest of the funds, 1.32 billion rupees has been raised as debt, he added.
Mathur said that the company hopes to stabilise the plant in the next couple of months by increasing yield. By the end of the year, the plant will be producing 100,000 mid-size tubes a month.
Yield is the number of error-free tubes produced per 100 tubes. The world wide average is in the range of 70 percent.
The capacity commissioned by LG-Hotline is only the first of three phases, which together will build up capacity to six million tubes by the turn of the century.

"The total investment in the plant will be 7.5 billion rupees, until 2000. After this line, we will add one by 1998 to make small size tubes, and another by 2000 to make large size tubes," Mathur said.
He added that the company should breakeven next year, as a yield of 57 percent to 58 percent will allow it to do so.

LG-Hotline's plant will sell tubes to television manufacturers catering to a market growing at below predictions. A study by management consultants Arthur D. Little in 1996 said the market would grow at 25 percent annually until 2000.

But according to government figures the growth has been only between 15 percent and 20 percent a year. In the 12 months to end March the total market for tubes was 2.6 million. This year it is expected to reach 3.0 million.

LG-Hotline will also have to compete against two established players, JCT Electronics Ltd and Samtel Colour Ltd, which have together been producing about 1.3 million tubes a year, and have had a hold on the domestic market.
The company is hedging its bets by targeting the Middle East and South Asian countries as export markets.

V.N. Masaldan, director, LG Hotline said, "Only half our production will be sold locally. The rest will be exported to markets that are geographically close to us, but tough for LG to support from Korea."
